questions.explain: The past perfect marks an action completed before another past moment.

questions.q: What is the past participle of *volver*?
questions.explain: Volver has the irregular participle vuelto.

questions.q: Choose the correct word order: "I had already seen it."
questions.explain: Pronouns go before haber and nothing separates haber from the participle.
When an -er/-ir stem ends in a vowel, -iendo becomes -yendo.
-ir verbs keep their preterite o→u stem change in the gerundio.
An -ing form used as a noun is translated with the infinitive in Spanish.
After haber the participle never changes.

questions.q: *___* aquí desde 2019. (I have lived here since 2019 and still do.)
questions.explain: Spanish uses the simple present for situations that continue up to now.
The future perfect expresses something completed by a future point.

questions.q: Juan no contesta. *___* dormido. (He must have fallen asleep.)
questions.explain: The future perfect can express a guess about something that has probably happened.
With passive se the verb agrees with the plural noun pisos.
Se vive has no subject noun and states what people in general do.
The ser passive uses the participle agreeing with the masculine singular subject.

questions.q: Las chicas con *___* viajé eran argentinas.
questions.explain: After a preposition, people are referred to with quien(es) (or las que).

questions.q: El autor, *___* novela ganó el premio, es colombiano.
questions.explain: Cuyo agrees with the thing possessed, here the feminine noun novela.

questions.q: Si lo hubiera sabido, te lo *___*.
questions.explain: The result of an unreal past condition goes in the conditional perfect.
A wish about another person's action takes the present subjunctive.

questions.q: What is the present subjunctive *nosotros* form of *dormir*?
questions.explain: -ir stem-changers change o to u in the nosotros and vosotros subjunctive forms.
Negated belief (no creer que) triggers the subjunctive.
A lo mejor is always followed by the indicative.
Cuando referring to the future takes the subjunctive.
An unknown, hypothetical antecedent takes the subjunctive in the relative clause.

questions.q: Me alegro de que *___*. (that you have come)
questions.explain: A present emotion about a completed action takes the present perfect subjunctive.

questions.q: Si *___* dinero, viajaría por el mundo.
questions.explain: Unreal present conditions use si + imperfect subjunctive, never the conditional.
A past trigger requires the imperfect subjunctive.

questions.q: Ojalá no *___* eso ayer. (I wish I hadn't said that.)
questions.explain: Regret about the past uses ojalá + past perfect subjunctive.
An action in progress interrupted by another past event uses the imperfect progressive.
The preterite progressive describes an ongoing action over a completed, defined period.
The future progressive expresses a guess about an action happening now.

questions.q: Si no lloviera, *___* jugando al tenis.
questions.explain: The conditional progressive describes what would be happening in a hypothetical situation.
